description.narrative:
UNICEF and Sida has a multiyear agreement (2025-2027) for a initiative run by UNICEF's Innovation Hub in Stockholm. The aim is to provide support to the female health tech industry in Africa, commonly known as FemTech. The initiative will be run by UNICEF's Innovation Hub in Stockholm and the Venture Fund.
The female health technology industry, focuses on leveraging technology to address women's health and wellbeing needs. In recent years, the FemTech industry has seen impressive growth encompassing technologies aimed at enhancing women and girls sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) with products, services, and solutions predominantly built for, by, and with women and girls. While there has been a notable growth in Femtech founders and solutions across the industry, limited attention has been paid to founder talent in emerging markets and designing solutions that solve the diverse health needs of women and girls in low and middle income countries.
The objective of this initiative is to: -Increase awareness and access to, and respect for, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for all, to empower girls and young women -Improve the availability and quality of healthcare products and services for girls and women -Increase investment flows to these solutions

UNICEF har lämnat in en ansökan till Sida om flerårig finansiering (2025–2027) för ett nytt initiativ som drivs av UNICEFs Innovation Hub i Stockholm. Målet är att ge stöd till den kvinnliga hälsoteknologiska industrin i Afrika, allmänt känd som FemTech. Initiativet kommer att drivas av UNICEFs Innovation Hub i Stockholm och den så kallade riskfonden. UNICEF ansöker om 45 000 000 kr för 20252027. Den kvinnliga hälsoteknikindustrin, fokuserar på att utnyttja tekniken för att ta itu med kvinnors behov av hälsa och välbefinnande. Under de senaste åren har FemTech industrin har sett en imponerande tillväxt som omfattar teknik som syftar till stärka kvinnors och flickors sexuella och reproduktiva hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) med produkter, tjänster och lösningar huvudsakligen byggda för, av och med kvinnor och flickor. Även om det har skett en anmärkningsvärd tillväxt av Femtech-grundare och lösningar inom branschen, begränsad uppmärksamhet har ägnats grundaren talang på framväxande marknader och designa lösningar som löser mångfalden hälsa kvinnors och flickors behov i låg- och medelinkomstländer. Målet med detta nya initiativ är att: Öka medvetenheten och tillgången till, och respekten för, sexuella och reproduktiva hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) för alla, för att stärka flickor och unga kvinnor Förbättra tillgängligheten och kvaliteten på sjukvårdsprodukter och tjänster för flickor och kvinnor; Öka investeringsflödena till dessa lösningar

UNICEF has submitted an application to Sida for multi­year funding (2025–2027) for a new initiative run by UNICEF's Innovation Hub in Stockholm. The aim is to provide support to the female health tech industry in Africa, commonly known as FemTech. The initiative will be run by UNICEF's Innovation Hub in Stockholm and the so­called Venture Fund. UNICEF is applying for SEK 45 000 000 for 2025­2027. The female health technology industry, focuses on leveraging technology to address women's health and wellbeing needs. In recent years, the FemTech industry has seen impressive growth encompassing technologies aimed at enhancing women and girl’s sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) with products, services, and solutions predominantly built for, by, and with women and girls. While there has been a notable growth in Femtech founders and solutions across the industry, limited attention has been paid to founder talent in emerging markets and designing solutions that solve the diverse health needs of women and girls in low and middle income countries. The objective of this new initiative is to: ­Increase awareness and access to, and respect for, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for all, to empower girls and young women ­Improve the availability and quality of healthcare products and services for girls and women; ­Increase investment flows to these solutions

During 2025 the Venture Fund completed its first call for applications. Out of approximately 1,200 startup applicants, 11 companies from seven countries were selected for support. The selected companies are developing technology-driven solutions aimed at improving the lives of girls and women in the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).
One of the selected companies is Kairos from Burkina Faso, which has developed the YouthShield app, a social media monitoring tool with a particular focus on identifying and countering misinformation related to gender equality and SRHR. Another example is the Tunisian company Feel by Luna, which has developed an AI-based application that allows users to record symptoms related to endometriosis. The purpose is to provide healthcare providers with better data for assessment, follow-up, and personalized care.
During 2026, the selected companies will work closely with the UNICEF Venture Fund and specially appointed mentors to further develop their products, strengthen implementation in their respective markets, and generate documented and measurable results for girls and women.
A new call for applications will start end of 2026.
